tagline: Down off Cleopatra Hill to the Verde Valley floor.
intro: The old road starts at the west end of Jerome, more than 5,000 feet up on Cleopatra Hill, a town that looks about to slip off the slope. Ten thousand people lived here in the 1920s. When the mines closed for good in 1953 fewer than a hundred stayed, and the galleries came later.

Below town the road winds down through Deception Gulch, with the Mogollon Rim out ahead, into Clarkdale. From there Historic 89A runs along Broadway past Tuzigoot and becomes Main Street in Cottonwood, ten miles in all.

moments.title: Jerome
moments.text: The copper here was among the richest ever found, though not inexhaustible. In the 1980s one company took $33 million in gold out of the Little Daisy, at a cost of $35 million.

moments.title: Clarkdale
moments.text: William Clark built it in 1912 as the smelter town for his Jerome mine, with telephones, sewers and spring water laid on, and the whole original town site is now on the National Register.

moments.title: Tuzigoot
moments.text: A Sinagua pueblo of 110 rooms along a ridge 120 feet above the Verde floodplain. The mining company sold the site to the county for a dollar so the excavation could go ahead.
